drills.q: EU-regulated bursty chatbot: which Azure OpenAI deployment type?
drills.a: Data Zone Standard (EU): processing confined to EU data zone with pay-per-token economics; Global would process anywhere (compliance fail); Regional pins one region and throttles painfully on bursts.

drills.q: PTU deployment creation fails despite available quota. Explain.
drills.a: Quota is a policy ceiling; capacity is physical compute held at deploy time and changes dynamically. Check the capacities API / alternate regions before promising dates - owning quota guarantees nothing.

drills.q: Launch day 429s on a shared deployment used by three features. Restructure.
drills.a: Split deployments per criticality with own TPM ceilings, batch work to Batch API, backoff+jitter everywhere, client concurrency caps, PTU for interactive path if steady economics justify, per-deployment token dashboards.

drills.q: Design permission-safe retrieval for 5M chunks with group-based access.
drills.a: AI Search S2-class, integrated vectorization, hybrid RRF fusion, semantic ranker gated to user-facing paths after measured lift; security-trim filter INSIDE queries (group list resolved server-side), never post-top-k filtering.

drills.q: Why does post-retrieval permission filtering leak?
drills.a: Top-k truncation happens first: forbidden items displace permitted ones users should have seen, and any pre-filter exposure bug is catastrophic. Permissions must enter the query as filter predicates.

drills.q: Agent conversation transcripts are regulated data. Basic or Standard setup?
drills.a: Standard: capability hosts binding your Cosmos DB (threads), AI Search (vectors), Blob (files) makes transcripts auditable/exportable/deletable under your retention policy; Basic keeps them Microsoft-side where erasure SLAs depend on platform APIs.

drills.q: Team fine-tuned a model and hallucinations increased. Why?
drills.a: Fine-tuning optimizes form not facts; baked-in knowledge goes stale and training-data errors get amplified confidently. Knowledge belongs in retrieval; fine-tune only format/style/behavior compression.

drills.q: Semantic ranker bill spiked but quality unchanged. What happened?
drills.a: Ranker applied to internal/low-value query paths without measuring lift; gate it to user-facing surfaces, A/B measure before paying, monitor free-allowance consumption and per-path usage.

drills.q: Shadow deployment on ML managed endpoint doubles costs - explain mechanics.
drills.a: Mirror mode executes candidate deployments fully on their instances for regression comparison without returning responses to users; budget limited soak windows or size candidates for doubled load rather than leaving mirrors on.

drills.q: Legitimate medical queries get content-filtered. Response plan?
drills.a: Tune severity thresholds within policy, provide grounded context helping classifiers, build escalation path for false positives, log filter-hit rates per surface; never disable filters wholesale - document residual-risk decisions instead.

drills.q: Explain AI Search's vector index quota model and its planning implication for a growing corpus.
drills.a: Vector quota is a memory constraint scaled per partition (roughly 35GB per partition for post-April-2024 S1 services) -- HNSW-indexed fields must reside fully in memory during queries. A growing vector corpus without partition-count planning hits the memory ceiling before any storage ceiling, since exhaustive KNN (which pages into memory dynamically) is the only vector field type that doesn't consume this quota.
